reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises. E2 describes SPS of high-entropy diborides, not HEA nanoparticle additions to ZrB2. E1 and E3 discuss mechanical properties of bulk CoCrNi and CoCrFeNi MEAs, not their use as sintering aids or their effect on ZrB2. E4 warns about phase instability of CoCrFeMnNi HEA, which contradicts the premise of stable, beneficial nanoparticle distribution. No evidence supports enhanced sintering, reduced porosity, or improved corrosion resistance in plating baths.
premises: CoCrFeMnNi HEA nanoparticles can be uniformly distributed at ZrB2 grain boundaries and within grains
Addition of 5 vol% HEA nanoparticles will enhance sintering kinetics and reduce porosity in ZrB2 at 1800 °C
The HEA addition will improve strength, toughness, and structural integrity of ZrB2
The HEA addition will reduce hole formation and failure during exposure to a liquid plating bath
Spark plasma sintering at 1800 °C with HEA is sufficient to densify the composite
